candidates.title: Fix Flowise 746 Chat Message Route (#6719)
candidates.security_relevance: Routes previously bound controllers with zero RBAC middleware: GET /api/v1/chat-messages/:id, DELETE /api/v1/chat-messages/ (removeAllChatMessages), PUT /api/v1/chat-messages/abort/:chatflowid/:chatid, GET /api/v1/internal-chat-messages/:id. Fix wraps all four in checkAnyPermission('chatflows:* / agentflows:* / assistants:delete'). Additionally, abort path has no workspace scoping at any layer: snapshot controller passes req.params.chatflowid/chatid straight to chatMessagesService.abortChatMessage(chatid, chatflowid), and the service builds `${chatflowid}_${chatId}` and calls abortControllerPool.abort(id) (or queue publishEvent) with no workspace/ownership check.

recovered.source: Authenticated HTTP requests: req.params.id / req.params.chatflowid / req.params.chatid on /api/v1/chat-messages* (any authenticated user of any role)
recovered.missing_guard: (1) checkAnyPermission RBAC middleware on all chat-message routes; (2) for abort specifically: any workspace/ownership assertion - ids are used raw to index the global abortControllerPool
recovered.sink: getAllChatMessages (read, workspace-scoped in controller), removeAllChatMessages (delete), abortControllerPool.abort(`${chatflowid}_${chatId}`) / QUEUE-mode publishEvent({eventName:'abort', id})
recovered.impact: RBAC bypass: roles without chatflows:view/delete can read and bulk-delete workspace chat history. Cross-workspace DoS: any authenticated user can abort another tenant's in-flight prediction streams by guessing/knowing chatflowid+chatid (ids also appear in public chat API responses).

candidates.snapshot_evidence: snapshot routes/chat-messages/index.ts lines 10/16 and internal-chat-messages/index.ts line 8 bind controllers with no middleware; services/chat-messages abortChatMessage has no workspaceId parameter; controllers/chat-messages abortChatMessage passes raw params

candidates.title: add: permissions for bullmq endpoint (#6713)
candidates.security_relevance: Bull Board dashboard mounted at /admin/queues previously chained only rateLimiter + verifyTokenForBullMQDashboard. Fix inserts checkPermission('admin:queues') (new admin permission, default off for non-admin roles) ahead of the Bull Board router.

recovered.source: Authenticated HTTP requests to /admin/queues* (any account passing verifyTokenForBullMQDashboard)
recovered.missing_guard: RBAC permission check - token validity was the only gate; no role/permission requirement for an admin-only surface
recovered.sink: Bull Board router: queue listing, job inspection (job payloads can embed chatflow inputs/credential-bearing node data), job retry/purge
recovered.impact: Non-admin authenticated users gain admin queue dashboard access: read job payloads (potential sensitive data disclosure) and manipulate/purge queues (availability impact) when QUEUE mode Bull Board is enabled.

candidates.snapshot_evidence: snapshot packages/server/src/index.ts line 350: this.app.use('/admin/queues', rateLimiter, verifyTokenForBullMQDashboard, this.queueManager.getBullBoardRouter()) - no checkPermission

candidates.title: fix: flowise-603 (#6708)
candidates.security_relevance: Credential lookups in openaiAssistantsService.getAllOpenaiAssistants / getSingleOpenaiAssistant / uploadFilesToAssistant and assistantsService.deleteAssistant used findOneBy({ id: credentialId }) with attacker-chosen credential id and NO workspaceId predicate; TTS getVoices had no workspace credential assertion (fix adds credentialsService.assertCredentialInWorkspace). Route fixes: /openai-assistants-files/upload gains checkAnyPermission('assistants:create,assistants:update') ordered BEFORE multer file parsing; /text-to-speech/voices gains checkAnyPermission('chatflows:config,agentflows:config').

recovered.source: req.query.credential (arbitrary credential UUID) on GET /api/v1/openai-assistants, GET /api/v1/openai-assistants/:id, POST /api/v1/openai-assistants-files/upload/, GET /api/v1/text-to-speech/voices?provider=&credential=
recovered.propagation: controller -> service -> AppDataSource.getRepository(Credential).findOneBy({ id: credentialId }) // no workspaceId -> decryptCredential(credential.credentialData) -> OpenAI/ElevenLabs client constructed with decrypted key
recovered.missing_guard: workspace-scoped credential lookup (workspaceId predicate / assertCredentialInWorkspace) and RBAC middleware on the upload + voices routes
recovered.sink: Outbound API calls executed with the victim workspace's decrypted API key; API responses (assistant listings, uploaded file ids, voice lists) returned to the attacker
recovered.impact: Cross-workspace credential access and use: any authenticated user can enumerate/use any credential id from another workspace - both data exposure (resource listings of the victim's OpenAI org) and financial/attribution abuse of stolen API keys (uploads, assistant ops). Unpermissioned multipart upload also let low-privilege/permissionless roles hit multer parsing.

candidates.snapshot_evidence: snapshot services/openai-assistants/index.ts lines 18-20, 46-48, 87-89: findOneBy({ id: credentialId }) only; routes/openai-assistants-files/index.ts and routes/text-to-speech/index.ts contain no checkAnyPermission; controllers pass only req.query.credential

candidates.title: fix: upsert history permissions (#6680)
candidates.security_relevance: GET and PATCH /api/v1/upsert-history had no RBAC middleware; fix adds checkAnyPermission('chatflows:view,documentStores:view') to GET and checkAnyPermission('chatflows:update,documentStores:upsert-config') to PATCH. (GET already enforced workspace scoping via getChatflowById; PATCH already called assertChatflowIdsInWorkspace - the fix additionally recognizes document-store ids as valid resources and keeps the workspace predicate.)

recovered.propagation: route (no permission middleware) -> upsertHistoryController -> upsertHistoryService (workspace-scoped queries)
recovered.missing_guard: checkAnyPermission RBAC middleware on both routes
recovered.sink: UpsertHistory read (document names, paths, statuses, uploader info) and delete
recovered.impact: RBAC bypass: roles without chatflows/documentStores permissions can read and delete upsert-history records within the workspace (audit-trail deletion, information disclosure about ingested documents). Lower severity than cross-workspace issues since workspace scoping existed.

candidates.snapshot_evidence: snapshot routes/upsert-history/index.ts lines 8/11: router.get / router.patch bind controller directly, no checkAnyPermission import

candidates.title: fix: flowise-708 (#6679)
candidates.security_relevance: SSOBase login handler: when a user found by email had status INVITED, the old code silently completed the invitation - it built a user object with status ACTIVE and called accountService.register(data), activating the account. Fix replaces this with a 403 USER_INVITED_PENDING_ACTIVATION. Commit comment states the rationale: invitation completion proves control of the emailed tempToken; an SSO login only proves the IdP's email assertion, which is not equivalent proof.

recovered.source: SSO login callback for an email that matches a user row with status=INVITED (email asserted by the identity provider; attacker-controlled if attacker has an IdP identity with the victim's email, or a second/misconfigured tenant IdP)
recovered.propagation: userService.readUserByEmail(email) -> user.status === INVITED -> accountService.register({ user: { ...user, email, status: ACTIVE, credential: undefined } }) -> user = newAccount.user
recovered.missing_guard: Proof-of-email-control requirement for invitation activation (tempToken link); SSO assertion was treated as equivalent
recovered.sink: Account activation followed by normal session/JWT issuance for the (now ACTIVE) invited user
recovered.impact: Authentication bypass / account pre-hijack: an attacker who can make an SSO IdP assert a victim's invited email activates that account and inherits the invited workspace/organization membership and role without ever controlling the invited mailbox.

candidates.snapshot_evidence: snapshot SSOBase.ts lines 81-92: if (user.status === UserStatus.INVITED) { ... const newAccount = await accountService.register(data); user = newAccount.user } - auto-activation present

candidates.title: fix: flowise-707 (#6712)
candidates.security_relevance: Introduces SSO identity binding: User gains ssoProvider/ssoSubjectId columns; on SSO login, if both are set and (provider, subjectId) does not match, login is rejected with SSO_IDENTITY_MISMATCH (404-family audit LoginActivityCode.INVALID_LOGIN_MODE recorded); on first SSO login the pair is bound via userService.bindSSOIdentity. Missing provider profile.id is rejected. Before this, SSO account matching was purely by email.

recovered.source: Email assertion from any configured SSO identity provider (profile.email) plus provider name; multi-IdP or tenant-admin-configurable SSO makes the asserted email attacker-influenced
recovered.propagation: userService.readUserByEmail(email) returns the victim's local/other-provider account; no binding check existed, so the SSO subject is accepted as that user
recovered.missing_guard: Binding of an account to its provenance (ssoProvider, ssoSubjectId) and mismatch rejection; equivalently: trust that IdP-asserted email == account ownership
recovered.sink: Session/JWT issuance for the matched existing user (full account takeover of login)
recovered.impact: Email-collision SSO account takeover: an attacker controlling an IdP identity that asserts a victim's email (second IdP, self-registered OIDC, tenant admin adds rogue IdP, or IdP without verified-email enforcement) logs in AS the victim, inheriting all workspaces/roles of that account.

candidates.snapshot_evidence: snapshot user.entity.ts has no ssoProvider/ssoSubjectId columns; SSOBase.ts matches user solely via readUserByEmail (line 56); no bindSSOIdentity/mismatch branch exists

candidates.title: Fix Flowise-552 Add Allow List Execution Path (#6658)
candidates.security_relevance: Replaces validateArgsForLocalFileAccess blocklist (regex dangerousPatterns: absolute-path prefixes, ../, ~/, file://, dangerous extensions, --file-family flags, null bytes, length cap) with a default-deny allowlist: args[0] (script path) must be an exact member of CUSTOM_MCP_ALLOWED_ABSOLUTE_SCRIPT_PATHS (comma-separated operator env var); empty/unset = execution disabled entirely. Blocklist approach was bypassable in principle (relative script paths not matching any pattern, extension-less interpreters/scripts, pattern-blind encodings).

recovered.source: MCP server config args array in chatflow node data (user-controlled via Flowise UI/API): serverParams.args -> validateArgsForLocalFileAccess(serverParams.args)
recovered.propagation: chatflow save/execute -> CustomMCP/Supergateway stdio transport -> spawn(command, args) where command gated by CUSTOM_MCP_ALLOWED_COMMANDS (f5d16835) but args were only blocklist-filtered
recovered.missing_guard: Allowlist on the executed script path (default-deny); blocklist regexes were the only filter
recovered.sink: stdio child process spawn of the attacker-influenced script path with remaining args
recovered.impact: Local file/script execution as the Flowise server process (RCE-adjacent) via blocklist bypass in stdio custom MCP args, when custom MCP stdio is enabled and security checks are not disabled.

candidates.snapshot_evidence: snapshot MCP/core.ts lines 181-215 implements the OLD blocklist validateArgsForLocalFileAccess (dangerousPatterns); CUSTOM_MCP_ALLOWED_ABSOLUTE_SCRIPT_PATHS and CUSTOM_MCP_ALLOWED_COMMANDS do not exist in snapshot code; note this is a hardening follow-up to known f5d16835 (same family, distinct commit)

candidates.title: Fix Flowise 849 SSO And Role (#6634)
candidates.security_relevance: LoginMethodController.testConfig previously performed no platform assertion and no organization match: fix prepends assertEnterprisePlatform() (403 on CLOUD/OPEN_SOURCE) and assertQueryOrganizationMatchesActiveOrg(user, req.body.organizationId). RoleService.updateRole gains an explicit organizationId mismatch rejection (404) in addition to the existing silent coercion newRole.organizationId = oldRole.organizationId.

recovered.source: POST /api/v1/login-methods/test body: { providers: [{config}], providerName, organizationId } (org admin with sso:manage); role update body organizationId
recovered.propagation: login-method route (checkPermission('sso:manage') only) -> testConfig used req.body.organizationId / provider configs with no cross-check against the caller's active organization; role.service accepted newRole.organizationId differing from the stored role's org (silently coerced at save, so the org-move itself was neutralized; the mismatch now 404s)
recovered.missing_guard: assertQueryOrganizationMatchesActiveOrg (cross-org confusion: org-A admin targeting org-B organizationId) and assertEnterprisePlatform (endpoint reachable on OSS/CLOUD platform types where enterprise SSO admin must not operate)
recovered.sink: SSO provider config test (outbound requests driven by req.body provider config, e.g. OIDC discovery/token endpoints); role persistence
recovered.impact: Cross-organization admin action: an organization admin could exercise SSO config testing under another organization's id (tenant confusion, outbound request primitive with attacker-influenced endpoints); on non-enterprise platform types the enterprise test endpoint was invocable. Role org-change portion was already coerced pre-fix (defense-in-depth only).

candidates.snapshot_evidence: snapshot login-method.controller.ts testConfig (line 162) starts directly with providers parsing - no assertEnterprisePlatform/assertQueryOrganizationMatchesActiveOrg calls (helpers exist in snapshot and are used by workspace/organization-user controllers); role.service.ts line 128 shows coercion-only handling

CUSTOM_MCP_SECURITY_CHECK_bypass.detail: Opt-out toggle unchanged on origin/main: CustomMCP.ts line 176 and SupergatewayMCP.ts line 109 still gate validation with `if (process.env.CUSTOM_MCP_SECURITY_CHECK !== 'false')`. What changed is the gated validation itself: origin/main validateMCPServerConfig is now default-deny allowlist-based (CUSTOM_MCP_ALLOWED_COMMANDS for the command, CUSTOM_MCP_ALLOWED_ABSOLUTE_SCRIPT_PATHS for args[0], cwd rejected outright, env vars allowlisted) per f5d16835 + e816d26a. So the bypass requires an operator to explicitly set CUSTOM_MCP_SECURITY_CHECK=false, after which all validation (allowlists included) is skipped.
CUSTOM_MCP_SECURITY_CHECK_bypass.snapshot_state: snapshot has the same toggle wrapping the weaker blocklist-era validation; snapshot grep: CustomMCP.ts:176, SupergatewayMCP.ts:109, commands/base.ts:108

NodeVM_dependency_escape_KU02.detail: origin/main availableDependencies in packages/components/src/utils.ts contains 60 entries and NO puppeteer or playwright; f20d0941 added explicit warning comments (launch() forwards executablePath/args into child_process.spawn -> sandbox escape; file:// navigation -> arbitrary host file read) and removed them from the commented TOOL_FUNCTION_EXTERNAL_DEP example in all .env.example files. The operator extension mechanism itself (TOOL_FUNCTION_EXTERNAL_DEP / ALLOW_BUILTIN_DEP) is unchanged by design: an operator can still allowlist arbitrary modules, which reintroduces the escape.
NodeVM_dependency_escape_KU02.snapshot_state: puppeteer/playwright not present in snapshot availableDependencies either; KU02 concerns the mechanism (operator-extendable NodeVM dependency list), which is unchanged in both
